question: Which two drugs are combined inside a single ampoule of Syntometrine?
explanation: Syntometrine is a fixed-dose combination medication containing both oxytocin and ergometrine maleate to manage the third stage of labor. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T3#BMP213_U1_T3_h1)

question: Why are two different drugs mixed together in Syntometrine?

options.A: Both drugs work at the exact same speed to relax the lower uterine segment
options.B: One provides immediate contraction while the other sustains the uterine tone
options.C: It completely eliminates all normal side effects associated with ergot alkaloids
options.D: It allows the medication to be safely taken by mouth instead of injection

explanation: Oxytocin works very fast to start contractions, while ergometrine takes a little longer but keeps the uterus firm over a longer period. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T3#BMP213_U1_T3_h1)

question: How does the ergometrine part of the drug help stop bleeding after birth?

options.A: By relaxing the cervical os to allow rapid passage of lochia
options.B: By lowering the general body temperature to slow down circulation
options.C: By dissolving any blood clots forming inside the uterine cavity
options.D: By causing a sustained tonic contraction that squeezes open blood vessels

explanation: Ergometrine makes the uterine muscle clamp down steadily. This action physically pinches off the open blood vessels where the placenta detached. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T3#BMP213_U1_T3_h2)

question: What effect can ergometrine have on a patient's blood pressure?

options.A: It remains completely unchanged because the drug targets only the uterus
options.B: It can rise significantly due to widespread blood vessel constriction
options.C: It fluctuates wildly in a rhythmic pattern matching the uterine contractions
options.D: It drops rapidly because blood pools inside the relaxed lower limbs

explanation: Ergometrine narrows blood vessels all over the body, which can cause blood pressure to go up. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T3#BMP213_U1_T3_h2)

question: When is Syntometrine primarily used in the labor ward?

options.A: Active management of the third stage of labor
options.B: Induction of labor in a post-term pregnancy
options.C: Relief of severe afterpains following delivery
options.D: Softening of an unfavorable cervix before induction

explanation: Syntometrine is given right after the baby is born to help deliver the placenta and prevent heavy bleeding. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T3#BMP213_U1_T3_h3)

question: At what exact point during delivery should a midwife give Syntometrine?

options.A: Four hours before the expected time of delivery to ripen the uterine muscles
options.B: Right after the delivery of the baby's anterior shoulder or newborn infant
options.C: During the latent phase of the first stage of labor to speed up cervical dilation
options.D: Only after manual removal of a retained placenta in the operating theatre

explanation: Giving it as the baby is born ensures it starts working right as the third stage begins. The midwife must first make sure there is no second baby. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T3#BMP213_U1_T3_h3)

question: What is the standard route of administration for a dose of Syntometrine?
explanation: Syntometrine is normally given as a single intramuscular injection to provide a steady and safe absorption rate. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T3#BMP213_U1_T3_h4)

question: Why is giving Syntometrine directly into a vein (IV bolus) discouraged?

options.A: It takes over thirty minutes to produce any noticeable clinical effect
options.B: It can cause a dangerous and sudden spike in the patient's blood pressure
options.C: It completely stops the oxytocin from working on the uterine muscle fibers
options.D: It causes the placenta to detach before the baby's head is even born

explanation: An intravenous injection of ergometrine causes blood vessels to narrow too quickly, leading to a dangerous spike in blood pressure. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T3#BMP213_U1_T3_h4)

question: Which of these conditions means a patient should NOT receive Syntometrine?
explanation: Giving Syntometrine to a patient with high blood pressure or preeclampsia is dangerous because it can raise their blood pressure even further. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T3#BMP213_U1_T3_h5)

question: A midwife is delivering twins. When is it safe to give Syntometrine?

options.A: Only after the second twin has been safely delivered
options.B: Immediately after the first twin's anterior shoulder appears
options.C: During the first stage of labor to speed up twin delivery
options.D: Before delivering either baby to prevent any blood loss

explanation: Syntometrine must never be given while another baby is still inside because strong contractions could harm the remaining twin. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T3#BMP213_U1_T3_h5)

question: What are two very common side effects after receiving Syntometrine?
explanation: Many patients feel nauseous or vomit shortly after receiving Syntometrine due to how ergot medicines affect the brain. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T3#BMP213_U1_T3_h6)

question: Why do patients often complain of strong cramp-like pains after a Syntometrine injection?

options.A: The drug causes intense, sustained contractions of the uterine muscle fibers
options.B: It forces the pelvic bones to rapidly separate back to pre-pregnancy size
options.C: It strips the inner lining of the stomach causing acute gastric ulcers
options.D: It causes severe dehydration by locking water inside the urinary bladder

explanation: The medicine makes the uterus contract very firmly, which naturally causes strong afterpains in the abdomen. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T3#BMP213_U1_T3_h6)

question: How should Syntometrine be stored to keep it working properly?

options.A: Submerged in sterile saline solution at body temperature
options.B: Refrigeration between 2°C and 8°C protected from light
options.C: Stored openly at room temperature in the delivery ward
options.D: Kept inside a dark freezer compartment below zero degrees

explanation: Syntometrine spoils easily if exposed to heat and light, so it must be kept in the refrigerator. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T3#BMP213_U1_T3_h7)

question: What is an essential check a midwife must perform after giving Syntometrine?

options.A: Palpating the uterine fundus to ensure it stays firm and contracted
options.B: Checking the newborn's sucking reflex during early breastfeeding
options.C: Measuring hourly urine output to check for renal tube blockage
options.D: Testing the client's visual acuity for signs of permanent blindness

explanation: The main goal of the drug is to keep the uterus hard, so the midwife must regularly feel the abdomen to confirm the uterus is contracted and bleeding is controlled. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T3#BMP213_U1_T3_h7)
